newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money easier after repo, reserve reqt.
newsitem.headline: German call money easier after repo, reserve reqt.

text.p: German call money rates eased to around three percent on Wednesday, helped by an injection of funds in the regular securities repurchase tender and increased certainty provided by the fixing of July's reserve requirement.
Call money was at 3.0 percent after Tuesday's 3.03/04.

The Bundesbank injected an additional 1.2 billion marks in the repo, alloting 72.1 billion marks at a fixed interest rate of three percent. The central bank also announced a provisional reserve requirement of 39.8 billion marks for June.
Dealers said the reserve requirement was in line with their expectations. Reserve holdings were comfortable, they said.

But dealers warned that the levels averall were still on the low side for complete fulfilment of the reserve quota over the month as a whole, adding this was likely to push call money back up above three percent by next week at the latest.
Banks held 41.6 billion marks in reserves on Tuesday for an average of 40.9 billion marks in the month to July 22.

With the dollar storming ahead to rates of almost 1.83 marks, some speculation returned to the market that the Bundesbank could tweak its securities repurchase rate higher at its regular council on Thursday. The central bank will also review its M3 money supply growth target at the meeting.

Dealers said a signal could be sent to markets either through a small increase in the securities repurchase rate or by the return to a floating rate securities repurhase tender, which effectively lets the market dictate the repo rate.
But changes in the discount and Lombard rate were all but ruled out, with 10 out of 10 economists in a Reuter poll this week saying they expected no change in the rates.

Economists and money market traders also said they expected the Bundesbank to leave its M3 growth target of 3-1/2 to 6-1/2 percent unchanged. M3 grew at an annualised monthly rate within the target range for the first time in June.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 3.03200 percent on Wednesday after 3.05667 percent on Tuesday.
Borrowing at the Lombard rate was negligible on Tuesday.
